newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico likely to bump up Cetes amount again - Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico likely to bump up Cetes amount again - Werner.

text.p: Mexico will likely continue to bump up the amount of treasury bills, or Cetes, that it offers at its weekly auctions, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said in an interview on Tuesday.

The increase of the auction amounts over the last two weeks will likely continue in order to meet the needs for financing the public budget deficit seen developing during the last half of the year, he said.
"In the next few weeks there will be a small additional increase, because we are adjusting the placements to meet financing requirements," he said.
Mexico increased the amount of Cetes on offer for the weekly auction this week to 4.2 billion pesos from 3.6 billion pesos the week before.
For most of the year the weekly amount had been stuck at 3.0 billion pesos.
Mexico posted a public sector surplus of 18.271 billion pesos in the first six months of the year, but government officials expect to end the year with a deficit of about 15.0 billion pesos.
